cli.help.short:
Commands: help [command] [-v|--verbose], mc, steam, terraria, exit
Servers use <game> server create|delete. For details, try help mc -v, help steam -v, or help terraria -v.
cli.help.short.mc:
Minecraft: mc server create|delete, mc api, mc versions, mc loaders, mc mod
Example: help mc server -v
cli.help.short.mc.api: API management: mc api list | add | remove
cli.help.short.mc.api.add: Add an API: mc api add <provider_type> ...
cli.help.short.mc.loaders: List Fabric Loader versions: mc loaders <fabric_api_id> <minecraft_version>
cli.help.short.mc.create: Create a server: mc server create <type> <version> <name> [api_id]
cli.help.short.mc.mod: Add Fabric mods or import a modpack ZIP: mc mod add <server_name> <source_path|pack.zip>
cli.help.short.steam:
Steam: steam server create|delete, steam mod, steam workshop
Example: help steam server -v
cli.help.short.steam.install: Create a Steam server: steam server create <app_id> <name>
cli.help.short.steam.mod: Steam mods: steam mod add or steam mod list
cli.help.short.steam.workshop: Left 4 Dead 2 Workshop: steam workshop item / collection / remove
cli.help.short.terraria:
Terraria: terraria server create|delete, terraria mod
Example: help terraria -v
cli.help.short.terraria.create: Create a server: terraria server create <type> <name>
cli.help.short.terraria.mod: Install tModLoader mods: terraria mod add or add-file
cli.help:
Available commands:
  help [command name]  Show detailed help (e.g. help steam server)
  mc server create <type> <version> <name> [api_id]
  mc server delete <name>
  mc api list | add | remove ...
  mc versions <api_id>
  mc loaders <fabric_api_id> <minecraft_version>
  mc mod add <name> <source_directory>
  steam server create <app_id> <name>
  steam server create <game> <name> <app_id>
  steam server delete <game> <name>
  steam mod add|list <game> <name> ...
  steam workshop item|collection|remove ...
  terraria server create <type> <name>
  terraria server delete <name>
  terraria mod add|add-file ...
  exit | quit
cli.help.minecraft:
Minecraft (mc) commands:
  mc server create <vanilla|fabric|forge|neoforge|paper> <version> <name> [api_id]
  mc server delete <name>
  mc api list | add | remove ...
  mc versions <api_id>
  mc loaders <fabric_api_id> <minecraft_version>
  mc mod add <name> <source_path>
Each provider type requires its own URLs. Vanilla APIs must follow Mojang's version_manifest_v2 format. See help mc api add for URL placeholders and details. Mods are copied into a Fabric server's mods/ folder. The older mc create form remains supported.
cli.help.steam:
Steam commands:
  steam server create <app_id> <name>
  steam server create <game> <name> <app_id>
  steam server delete <game> <name>
  steam mod add <game> <name> <source_path> [destination]
  steam mod list <game> <name> [destination]
  steam workshop item|collection|remove ...
Mods copy local files. Workshop commands are for Left 4 Dead 2 only and accept comma-separated numeric IDs and Steam Community URLs. steam install remains a supported alias.
cli.help.terraria:
Terraria commands:
  terraria server create <vanilla|tmodloader> <name>
  terraria server delete <name>
  terraria mod add <name> <workshop_id> <mod_name>
  terraria mod add-file <name> <file.tmod>
Vanilla installs the Terraria server; tmodloader installs the tModLoader server. Mod commands require a tModLoader server. Use the Workshop item's numeric ID and the mod's internal name (the name stored in tModLoader's enabled.json). Local .tmod files are copied into Mods and enabled automatically. Terraria and tModLoader are installed through SteamCMD; use [steam].login_mode = "account" for games that require an owned Steam account. The older terraria create form remains supported.
cli.help.terraria.mod:
Install tModLoader mods:
  terraria mod add <server_name> <workshop_id> <mod_name>
  terraria mod add-file <server_name> <file.tmod>
The Workshop form downloads the item with SteamCMD and registers its ID in Mods/install.txt and internal name in Mods/enabled.json. Find the internal name in the enabled.json exported from the tModLoader Mod Packs menu. The local-file form copies a .tmod file into Mods and enables its filename stem.
cli.help.short.server.delete: Delete a server: <game> server delete <name> (Steam also requires <game> before the server name)
cli.help.server.delete:
Delete server files permanently:
  mc server delete <name>
  steam server delete <game> <name>
  terraria server delete <name>
The exact server name must be typed to confirm the deletion.
cli.help.mc.api: Manage Minecraft APIs with mc api list, add, and remove. See help mc api add for syntax.
cli.help.mc.api.add:
Register an API:
  mc api add <provider_type> <api_id> <name> <endpoint_url...>
  vanilla <api_id> <name> <manifest_url>
  fabric <api_id> <name> <loader_url> <installer_versions_url> <installer_download_url>
  forge <api_id> <name> <promotions_url> <installer_download_url>
  neoforge <api_id> <name> <versions_url> <installer_download_url>
  paper <api_id> <name> <project_url> <version_builds_url>
api_id must be unique in the registry. Provide the required number and order of URLs for the selected provider_type. Fabric URLs use {minecraft_version} and {version}; Forge installer URLs use {minecraft_version} and {forge_version}; NeoForge installer URLs use {version}; Paper builds URLs use {minecraft_version}.
cli.help.mc.versions:
List Minecraft versions:
  mc versions <api_id>
Fetches the available versions from the selected API.
cli.help.mc.loaders:
List Fabric Loader versions:
  mc loaders <fabric_api_id> <minecraft_version>
Lists Fabric Loader versions available for the selected Minecraft version.
cli.help.mc.create:
Create a server:
  mc server create <vanilla|fabric|forge|neoforge|paper> <version> <server_name> [api_id]
Delete a server:
  mc server delete <server_name>
Deletion requires typing the exact server name and permanently removes its files. If api_id is omitted, vanilla uses mojang and other types use their same-named default API. Specify api_id to use a custom API. Forge and NeoForge generate launcher scripts; other types generate a server JAR launcher. The older mc create form remains supported.
cli.help.mc.mod:
Add Fabric mods or import a Prism/Modrinth ZIP:
  mc mod add <server_name> <source_file|directory|modpack.zip>
A ZIP imports server-side JARs from its Modrinth index download URLs or bundled mods folders. A successful import replaces the server's mods/ folder; files are verified before replacement. CurseForge manifest-only packs need downloads bundled in the ZIP.
cli.help.steam.install:
Create a Steam server:
  steam server create <app_id> <server_name>
  steam server create <game> <server_name> <app_id>
Delete a server:
  steam server delete <game> <server_name>
The short form uses the App ID as the game folder (servers/<app_id>/<server_name>). Use the three-argument form to choose a game folder name. Deletion requires typing the exact server name and permanently removes its files. steam install remains a supported alias.
With login_mode = "anonymous" in config.toml, it uses anonymous login; with "account", it uses the Steam username you enter. Enter your password and Steam Guard code in SteamCMD's interactive prompts.
cli.help.steam.mod:
Manage Steam mods:
  steam mod add <game> <server_name> <source_path> [destination]
  steam mod list <game> <server_name> [destination]
See help steam mod add or help steam mod list for details.
cli.help.steam.mod.add:
Add mods:
  steam mod add <game> <server_name> <source_path> [destination]
Copies local mod files or folders into destination within the server directory.
cli.help.steam.mod.list:
List mods:
  steam mod list <game> <server_name> [destination]
Lists files at the selected destination.
cli.help.steam.workshop:
Left 4 Dead 2 Workshop:
  steam workshop item <game> <server_name> <id_or_url>[,...]
  steam workshop collection <game> <server_name> <id_or_url>[,...]
  steam workshop remove item|collection <game> <server_name> <id_or_url>[,...]
Use comma-separated numeric IDs and Steam Community URLs. Existing files are confirmed before overwrite, and stale files are confirmed before deletion. item downloads the requested items in one SteamCMD run, expanding collection URLs or collection:ID references. collection expands nested collections and synchronizes every collection registered in the server's addons.lst. It compares update metadata and downloads only new or changed items. remove item deletes local files and sync metadata for the selected item; a registered collection may reinstall it during a later sync. remove collection unregisters the collection and removes managed VPKs not used by another registered collection. For items requiring a Steam account, set [steam].login_mode = "account".
